title: Kratka's Caravan dances and Papa Mutt's visit
summary: Blumberg describes the Saturday dances at the Caravan Kratka sponsored, leading when Bunk was weak, and Bunk playing superbly when Papa Mutt came.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, she had her followers and when a few people would come in that liked to hear her sing, she'd get up and sing with the band and sang very well. I know I never heard her. There was a time when...well, there was this job that we played with Bunk with...I guess it was Al Nicholas on clarinet. And I'm not clear on the personnel because it started out, I think it was a weekly Saturday night dance thing. Kratka himself sponsored this and we had two trumpets and the rest was standard New Orleans instrumentation. And later on it worked into a thing where they had two bands alternating, see, so that the personnel changed slightly. But, uh, the...I don't remember which time it was. There was one time, it might have been the first or second, uh, of these dances that, uh, uh, Bunk wasn't feeling too well. He got there late and, and, uh, he was hardly playing and, and he was telling me, go ahead, you take the lead and you do it, you know, you run the thing. And, uh, I was sweating, you know.
But this caravan, those dances were...was Bunk supposed to be there for all of those or was that your band or what was it? I don't remember. Well, uh...it wasn't there.
It was Kratka's band and, and he hired, uh, uh, Bunk and, and everybody else. Bunk was just, just had that time open and took the job. Yeah.
Bunk was supposed to be there regularly then. Yeah. It wasn't just as a start of special guest once a month or something.

No, well, it was, it was just a once a week thing anyway. Yeah. And, you know, it was like, it was like a jazz concert on a Saturday night with dancing. But, uh, uh, anyway, he told me to, to take over and I, I tried, you know, I did the best I could. But the next week, uh, Papa Mutt was there in the audience and he, he was visiting from, from the West Coast. And I guess he had heard stories about how Bunk was falling down on the job sometimes, you know, and, and he was probably hoping to, that he, uh, maybe be needed, you know, and get a chance to sit in. And, uh, uh, Bunk was playing more strongly than I've ever heard him before or since. I mean, it was a fantastic, uh, lip he had that night. He was, he was, uh, shaking high notes like a big band lead trumpet player, except that he was still had that beautiful tone of his. Yeah. And, uh, uh, I mean, I just, just about didn't blow my horn all night. I was just sitting there with a mouth hanging open and, and, uh, Bunk was playing in a, actually in a slightly different style from the style I'd been used to. It was somewhere between his regular style and Louie's style. Uh, it was, uh, and he was singing tunes. He was really feeling fine. And, and wherever Mutt would be dancing in the room, uh, Papa Mutt's very graceful dancer. Yeah. And, uh, uh, uh, wherever Mutt would be dancing, Bunk's horn would be pointed right, right at that spot, you know. And, uh, it was kind of funny to see that. But, uh, Bunk was just blowing beautifully. And, and I, at some point in the evening I said, uh, Bunk, you're just playing so great, you know. And, uh, he said, well, he says, I'm just paying you back the favor. He says, you filled in for me last week, and so I'm, I'm helping you out this week. He said. You know. He was probably really thinking about Mutt a good deal, too. Yeah, sure, sure. He was just fighting his arm.
